diff --git a/scripts/hive-launch b/scripts/hive-launch
index cb9529c..a141535 100755
--- a/scripts/hive-launch
+++ b/scripts/hive-launch
@@ -132,9 +132,22 @@ fi
 # Clobber guards: never overwrite an existing clone or a same-named live pane.
 [ ! -e "$WS_ROOT" ]   || die "$WS_ROOT already exists; pick a fresh --worker id or clear it"
 [ ! -e "$CODE_ROOT" ] || die "$CODE_ROOT already exists; pick a fresh --worker id or clear it"
+# The pane NAME is the registry (Phase 1 refuses a registry file), and tmux itself
+# happily creates a second window with the same name — so this guard is the only
+# thing standing between one task and two panes claiming to be it. It is the ONE
+# collision that survives name-only allocation, and it is a refusal, never a second
+# window: which of the two panes is the task becomes unanswerable.
 if tmux has-session -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null \
    && tmux list-windows -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | grep -qxF "$TASK"; then
-  die "a tmux window named '$TASK' already exists in session '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' (the pane is the registry)"
+  {
+    echo "hive-launch: a tmux window named '$TASK' already exists in session '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' — the pane IS the registry, so a second one is refused."
+    echo "  Recovery depends on what that window is:"
+    echo "    - a live or dead worker on this task: kill the pane, then recover with task.reassigned"
+    echo "      (RUNBOOK, 'Dead worker recovery') — a relaunch is not recovery and the board will refuse it."
+    echo "    - debris (a window that outlived its worker, no board state): kill it, then re-run this launch."
+    echo "      tmux kill-window -t '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION:$TASK'"
+  } >&2
+  exit 1
 fi
 
 # --- pin the order and build the seed payloads --------------------------------
@@ -225,16 +238,88 @@ Container tooling is podman (not docker). Begin by reading both files, then emit
 task.accepted and start.
 KICK
 
+# --- fail-safe for anything that fails AFTER the board writes ------------------
+# The board now owns the task (assigned, on the board, kickoff never delivered)
+# while the pane does not exist: a HALF-LAUNCH. Found by use 2026-07-27, where
+# reconstructing the missing half took WORKER.md §Launch plus the launch output
+# read by hand. The launcher knows every value that reconstruction needs, so it
+# prints the manual completion path instead of leaving it to archaeology.
+half_launch() {  # half_launch <what-failed>
+  {
+    echo
+    echo "hive-launch: HALF-LAUNCHED '$TASK' — $1"
+    echo "  The board already owns this task on run '$RUN' (task.assigned emitted); only the pane is missing."
+    echo "  Do NOT re-run hive-launch: it refuses an owned task, and a relaunch is not recovery (RUNBOOK)."
+    echo "  Everything else is in place:"
+    echo "    workspace clone: $WS_ROOT"
+    echo "    code clone:      $CODE_ROOT"
+    echo "    emit wrapper:    $WRAPPER"
+    echo "    kickoff text:    $KICKOFF_FILE"
+    echo
+    echo "  Finish the launch by hand (WORKER.md 'Launch (operator side)'; RUNBOOK 'Half-launched task'):"
+    echo "  1. Open the worker's window and start the session — one command, kickoff read from the file:"
+    cat <<CMD
+       tmux new-window -a -t '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION:{end}' -n '$TASK' -c '$WS_ROOT' \\
+         -e HIVE_KICKOFF="\$(cat '$KICKOFF_FILE')" '$HIVE_WORKER_CMD "\$HIVE_KICKOFF"'
+     (if session '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' does not exist, create it instead:)
+       tmux new-session -d -s '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' -n '$TASK' -c '$WS_ROOT' \\
+         -e HIVE_KICKOFF="\$(cat '$KICKOFF_FILE')" '$HIVE_WORKER_CMD "\$HIVE_KICKOFF"'
+     (or, from an attached client: prefix-c, then)
+       cd '$WS_ROOT' && $HIVE_WORKER_CMD "\$(cat '$KICKOFF_FILE')"
+CMD
+    echo "  2. The kickoff that command delivers (verbatim, so it can also be pasted into a running session):"
+    echo "  ----- kickoff -----"
+    printf '%s\n' "$KICKOFF" | sed 's/^/  /'
+    echo "  ----- end kickoff -----"
+    echo "  3. To abandon this launch instead: the task is owned, so recovery is task.reassigned"
+    echo "     (RUNBOOK, 'Dead worker recovery'), and clear $WORK_ROOT/$WORKER before reusing the worker id."
+  } >&2
+  exit 1
+}
+
+# The kickoff is also written to a file next to the worker's trees: it is what a
+# manual completion pastes if the pane step fails, and it costs nothing on the
+# happy path. Written through half_launch's guard like every other post-seeding
+# step — a failure here is a half-launch too, and the print carries the kickoff
+# verbatim, so the recovery survives even without the file.
+KICKOFF_FILE="$WORK_ROOT/$WORKER/kickoff.txt"
+printf '%s\n' "$KICKOFF" > "$KICKOFF_FILE" \
+  || half_launch "could not write the kickoff file $KICKOFF_FILE"
+
 # Open the pane. The kickoff travels as an env var (HIVE_KICKOFF) so no multi-line
 # text is ever quoted onto a command line; the window runs the worker command with
 # it as the initial prompt. The pane NAME is the registry — no registry file.
+#
+# Allocation is BY NAME ONLY: we supply the session and the window name (the task
+# id), never an index — the index carries no meaning and must never be chosen by
+# us. `-a` against `{end}` (the session's highest-numbered window) is append
+# semantics: tmux allocates the next index ABOVE the last one, which is free by
+# construction, so `create window failed: index N in use` (2026-07-27) cannot
+# happen. Two things this is deliberately NOT:
+#   * an explicit derived index — the original defect;
+#   * a bare `-t <session>` with the index omitted — that still resolves target
+#     to a concrete index: it fills the lowest FREE slot, dropping the worker
+#     window into the middle of the operator's window order, and the 2026-07-27
+#     recovery saw it fail identically to the explicit form. Index omission is
+#     not the fix; append semantics are.
+# `-a -t <session>` alone would insert after the session's CURRENT window and
+# shuffle the operator's own windows up; `{end}` appends past the last window, so
+# no existing window moves. Nothing here assumes a base-index or renumber-windows
+# setting: the allocation is relative to whatever indices the session already has.
 launch_cmd="$HIVE_WORKER_CMD \"\$HIVE_KICKOFF\""
 if tmux has-session -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null; then
-  tmux new-window -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" -n "$TASK" -c "$WS_ROOT" \
-    -e HIVE_KICKOFF="$KICKOFF" "$launch_cmd"
+  tmux new-window -a -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION:{end}" -n "$TASK" -c "$WS_ROOT" \
+    -e HIVE_KICKOFF="$KICKOFF" "$launch_cmd" \
+    || half_launch "tmux new-window failed in session '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' (see the tmux error above)"
 else
   tmux new-session -d -s "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" -n "$TASK" -c "$WS_ROOT" \
-    -e HIVE_KICKOFF="$KICKOFF" "$launch_cmd"
+    -e HIVE_KICKOFF="$KICKOFF" "$launch_cmd" \
+    || half_launch "tmux new-session failed for session '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' (see the tmux error above)"
 fi
+# Trust nothing about the pane: assert it exists. A window whose command died on
+# startup is a half-launch too, and it must reach the operator as one.
+tmux list-windows -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | grep -qxF "$TASK" \
+  || half_launch "the window was created but is already gone (did '$HIVE_WORKER_CMD' exit immediately?)"
 echo "  pane:   $HIVE_TMUX_SESSION:$TASK  (attach: tmux attach -t $HIVE_TMUX_SESSION)"
+echo "  kickoff: $KICKOFF_FILE"
 echo "hive-launch: done."
diff --git a/scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh b/scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh
index abe7595..4e55682 100755
--- a/scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh
+++ b/scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh
@@ -19,6 +19,11 @@
 # in the same events table under distinct run_ids, which auto-register — harmless
 # debris in separate runs. Do NOT put `omegahive` in any conf here.
 #
+# Nor the operator's tmux server: TMUX_TMPDIR moves the default socket into the
+# sandbox, so the drill's windows — including the deliberately hostile ones the
+# pane-allocation section builds — live on a private, throwaway server, never on
+# the one holding the live worker panes.
+#
 # Usage: scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh   (run from anywhere; needs podman + the stack up)
 
 set -euo pipefail
@@ -27,6 +32,15 @@ SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
 STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
 SANDBOX="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/hive-drill-${STAMP}.XXXXXX")"
 TMUX_SESSION="drill-${STAMP}"
+
+# tmux isolation — set before ANY tmux call, here or in the scripts under test.
+# The drill occupies indices, flips base-index/renumber-windows, and kills its
+# server at exit; doing that on the operator's default server would put every live
+# worker pane in the blast radius. TMUX_TMPDIR relocates the default socket, so a
+# plain `tmux` (which is what hive-launch calls) reaches the sandbox server only.
+export TMUX_TMPDIR="$SANDBOX/tmux"
+mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"
+unset TMUX   # running the drill from inside a tmux client must not leak that client's server
 OMEGA_DIR_REAL="${OMEGA_DIR:-$HOME/src/SNET/omegahive}"   # the real stack dir (compose + pg live here)
 
 # The two scratch projects and their runs (run id = project name convention, but
@@ -51,7 +65,9 @@ expect_fail_msg(){
 }
 
 cleanup() {
-  tmux kill-session -t "$TMUX_SESSION" 2>/dev/null || true
+  # kill-server, not kill-session: this is the sandbox's own server (TMUX_TMPDIR),
+  # so everything the drill created — every session, every occupant window — goes.
+  tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null || true
   rm -rf "$SANDBOX"
   echo
   echo "drill: runs=$ARUN,$BRUN  PASS=$PASS  FAIL=$FAIL  (scratch events remain under those runs)"
@@ -357,6 +373,101 @@ expect_fail_msg "launch refuses a done task (not launchable)" "not launchable" \
   "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch" "$AORDER" --worker "sess-adopt-done-${STAMP}"
 check "adopt refusal emitted no board state" "[ ! -e '$WORK/sess-adopt-done-${STAMP}' ]"
 
+# ==============================================================================
+echo
+echo "== pane allocation: occupied indices, name collision, half-launch recovery =="
+# The 2026-07-27 launch seeded all three spine events and then died on
+# `create window failed: index 4 in use`, stranding a half-launched task. Four
+# assertions: the hazard is still real on this tmux, name-only allocation is
+# immune to it under any config, the one surviving collision (the NAME) refuses
+# instead of doubling the pane, and a pane failure after seeding prints the
+# manual completion path.
+
+# (i) Build the hazard: occupy a run of indices and leave the CURRENT window in
+#     the middle (so an append-after-current form would shuffle the others up).
+for i in 1 2 3; do
+  tmux new-window -d -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -n "occupant-$i" 'sleep 600' >/dev/null 2>&1
+done
+IDXS=$(tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_index}' | sort -n)
+MAXIDX=$(printf '%s\n' "$IDXS" | tail -1)
+MIDIDX=$(printf '%s\n' "$IDXS" | head -2 | tail -1)
+tmux select-window -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$MIDIDX"
+expect_fail_msg "reproduction: creating at an explicit occupied index still fails (the 0727 defect)" "in use" \
+  tmux new-window -d -t "$TMUX_SESSION:$MAXIDX" -n repro-occupied 'sleep 600'
+
+# (ii) A real launch into exactly that state must allocate a free slot ABOVE the
+#      highest index and disturb no existing window.
+OORDER=$(add_order "$APROJ" "2026-07-13-drill-occupied" "occupied index")
+OWORKER="sess-occupied-${STAMP}"
+PANES_BEFORE=$(tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_index}:#{window_name}' | sort)
+"$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch" "$OORDER" --worker "$OWORKER" >/dev/null
+PANES_AFTER=$(tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_index}:#{window_name}' | sort)
+NEWIDX=$(tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_index} #{window_name}' | awk '$2=="drill-occupied"{print $1}')
+MOVED=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$PANES_BEFORE") <(printf '%s\n' "$PANES_AFTER") | tr '\n' ' ')
+check "occupied indices: launch created the window by name" "[ -n '$NEWIDX' ]"
+check "occupied indices: allocated above the highest index (append, never a chosen index)" \
+  "[ '${NEWIDX:-0}' -gt '$MAXIDX' ]"
+check "occupied indices: no existing window moved or was renamed" "[ -z '$MOVED' ]"
+check "occupied indices: board reached assigned"  "[ \"\$(bstatus '$ARUN' drill-occupied)\" = assigned ]"
+
+# (iii) The stop-line: allocation by name must hold under ANY tmux config, so run
+#       one launch with a hostile base-index and renumber-windows on.
+tmux set-option -g base-index 11 >/dev/null
+tmux set-option -g renumber-windows on >/dev/null
+BORDER2=$(add_order "$APROJ" "2026-07-13-drill-baseindex" "hostile base-index")
+"$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch" "$BORDER2" --worker "sess-baseidx-${STAMP}" >/dev/null
+check "hostile base-index + renumber-windows: window still created by name" \
+  "tmux list-windows -t '$TMUX_SESSION' -F '#{window_name}' | grep -qxF drill-baseindex"
+check "hostile base-index + renumber-windows: board reached assigned" \
+  "[ \"\$(bstatus '$ARUN' drill-baseindex)\" = assigned ]"
+tmux set-option -g renumber-windows off >/dev/null
+tmux set-option -g base-index 0 >/dev/null
+
+# (iv) The one collision name-only allocation cannot remove: a window already
+#      named for this task. tmux itself creates duplicate names happily, so this
+#      guard is the only thing keeping one task from having two panes.
+CORDER=$(add_order "$APROJ" "2026-07-13-drill-panecoll" "pane collision")
+tmux new-window -d -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -n drill-panecoll 'sleep 600'
+expect_fail_msg "an existing window with the task's name refuses the launch" "already exists" \
+  "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch" "$CORDER" --worker "sess-panecoll-${STAMP}"
+expect_fail_msg "name-collision refusal names the recovery path (task.reassigned)" "task.reassigned" \
+  "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch" "$CORDER" --worker "sess-panecoll-${STAMP}"
+NPANES=$(tmux list-windows -t "$TMUX_SESSION" -F '#{window_name}' | grep -cxF drill-panecoll)
+check "name collision created no second window"  "[ '$NPANES' = 1 ]"
+check "name collision provisioned nothing"       "[ ! -e '$WORK/sess-panecoll-${STAMP}' ]"
+check "name collision seeded no board state"     "[ -z \"\$(bstatus '$ARUN' drill-panecoll)\" ]"
+
+# (v) Fail-safe half-launch: force the pane step to fail exactly as it did on
+#     2026-07-27 with a PATH shim (the launcher calls plain `tmux`, so no seam is
+#     needed in production code) and assert the recovery print, not archaeology.
+REAL_TMUX=$(command -v tmux)
+SHIMDIR="$SANDBOX/shim"; mkdir -p "$SHIMDIR"
+cat > "$SHIMDIR/tmux" <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# drill shim: fail new-window with the historical message; pass everything else through.
+[ "\$1" = new-window ] && { echo "create window failed: index 4 in use" >&2; exit 1; }
+exec "$REAL_TMUX" "\$@"
+EOF
+chmod +x "$SHIMDIR/tmux"
+HORDER=$(add_order "$APROJ" "2026-07-13-drill-halflaunch" "half launch")
+HWORKER="sess-halflaunch-${STAMP}"
+HALF_RC=0
+HALF_OUT=$(PATH="$SHIMDIR:$PATH" "$SCRIPT_DIR/hive-launch" "$HORDER" --worker "$HWORKER" 2>&1) || HALF_RC=$?
+printf '%s\n' "$HALF_OUT"
+check "half-launch: the launcher exits non-zero when the pane fails" "[ $HALF_RC -ne 0 ]"
+check "half-launch: the strand is real (board owns it, no pane)" "[ \"\$(bstatus '$ARUN' drill-halflaunch)\" = assigned ]"
+check "half-launch: no window was created" \
+  "! tmux list-windows -t '$TMUX_SESSION' -F '#{window_name}' | grep -qxF drill-halflaunch"
+check "half-launch: the output names it a half-launch"   "printf '%s' \"\$HALF_OUT\" | grep -qF 'HALF-LAUNCHED'"
+check "half-launch: forbids a re-run as recovery"        "printf '%s' \"\$HALF_OUT\" | grep -qF 'Do NOT re-run hive-launch'"
+check "half-launch: prints the filled kickoff text"      "printf '%s' \"\$HALF_OUT\" | grep -qF 'You are hive worker $HWORKER on task drill-halflaunch'"
+check "half-launch: the printed kickoff names the wrapper" "printf '%s' \"\$HALF_OUT\" | grep -qF '$WRAPPERS/$HWORKER.sh'"
+check "half-launch: prints the manual pane command"      "printf '%s' \"\$HALF_OUT\" | grep -qF 'tmux new-window -a -t'"
+check "half-launch: prints the abandon path (task.reassigned)" "printf '%s' \"\$HALF_OUT\" | grep -qF 'task.reassigned'"
+check "half-launch: kickoff also saved to a file"        "[ -s '$WORK/$HWORKER/kickoff.txt' ]"
+check "half-launch: clones survive for the manual finish" "[ -d '$WORK/$HWORKER/hive/.git' ]"
+check "half-launch: wrapper survives for the manual finish" "[ -x '$WRAPPERS/$HWORKER.sh' ]"
+
 echo
 echo "== refusal paths =="
 # (a) dirty order — an uncommitted new order refuses at pin time.

--- a/projects/omegahive/RUNBOOK.md
+++ b/projects/omegahive/RUNBOOK.md
@@ -29,7 +29,10 @@ project, `WS_HUB`, `OPS_WS`, `WORK_ROOT`, `WRAPPER_DIR`, `HIVE_TMUX_SESSION`, `H
 `HIVE_RUN_ID` is the run escape hatch (wins over a conf's `RUN_ID`; the drill points it at a

 `scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh` — it drives the full lifecycle and every refusal path against a
-throwaway sandbox and a scratch run id (never the durable `omegahive` run).
+throwaway sandbox and a scratch run id (never the durable `omegahive` run), on its own private
+tmux server (`TMUX_TMPDIR` inside the sandbox, killed at exit) — so it never touches the `hive`

@@ -136,6 +139,43 @@ replaced, never resurrected:
 The board keeps the full history (both workers' events remain); no override is needed —
 the reassignment IS the recovery.
 
+### Half-launched task (the board owns it, no pane exists)
+
+`hive-launch` seeds the board before it opens the pane — deliberately, so the worker's
+first act (`task.accepted`) is legal the moment its session starts. The cost of that
+ordering is one failure mode: if the pane step fails, the task is owned on the board with
+no session and the kickoff never delivered. **This is not a dead worker** — no worker ever
+ran — so the reassignment path above is the wrong tool.
+
+You will know it by the launcher's own output: it exits non-zero and prints
+`hive-launch: HALF-LAUNCHED <task>` followed by the complete manual completion path. The
+board shows the task `assigned`, and `tmux list-windows -t hive` shows no window named for
+it. Everything else is already in place: both clones, the emit wrapper, and the filled
+kickoff saved at `~/work/<worker>/kickoff.txt`.
+
+**Do not re-run `hive-launch`** — the task is owned, so it refuses, and relaunch is not
+recovery.
+
+Finish it by hand — the launcher prints these commands filled in; this is the same thing
+from memory if the output has scrolled away (`$HIVE_WORKER_CMD`, default `claude`):
+
+```bash
+W=<worker>; T=<task>
+tmux new-window -a -t 'hive:{end}' -n "$T" -c ~/work/$W/hive \
+  -e HIVE_KICKOFF="$(cat ~/work/$W/kickoff.txt)" 'claude "$HIVE_KICKOFF"'
+# or, from an attached client: prefix-c, then
+#   cd ~/work/$W/hive && claude "$(cat ~/work/$W/kickoff.txt)"
+```
+
+The `-a -t 'hive:{end}'` form is append semantics: the window lands above the session's
+highest index, which is free by construction. Never name an explicit index — an occupied
+one is exactly the failure that produces a half-launch (2026-07-27), and the window *name*
+is the registry.
+
+To abandon the launch instead of finishing it: the task is owned, so retire it the same way
+a dead worker is replaced — register a fresh worker id and `task.reassigned` (above) — and
+clear `~/work/<worker>/` before reusing the id.
+
 ## Backups and restore
 
 Two stores, one backup directory. Losing the workspace is losing the project the same as
diff --git a/projects/omegahive/reports/2026-07-27-launch-pane-fix-result.md b/projects/omegahive/reports/2026-07-27-launch-pane-fix-result.md

--- /dev/null
+++ b/projects/omegahive/reports/2026-07-27-launch-pane-fix-result.md
@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@
+# Result — launch-pane-fix: tmux window by name, fail-safe half-launch
+
+**Task:** `launch-pane-fix` · **Order:** `projects/omegahive/orders/2026-07-27-launch-pane-fix.md`
+**Code:** branch `launch-pane-fix` in the omegahive code repo — commits `68e5ed8`, `79301f5`,
+branched from merged main at `e9656a4`. That base already carries the project-config refactor
+(`project.conf` / `load_project_conf` / `CANON_ROOT` / the portfolio-wide review throttle), which
+is what the order's sequencing clause waits on; no `projects/omegahive/reports/` entry exists in
+this workspace copy, so project-config's own result report is cited by name, not by pin.
+
+## What shipped
+
+One PR touching two files in `scripts/`, plus the RUNBOOK section the order names.
+
+**1. Window allocation is by name only (`scripts/hive-launch`).** The pane step is now
+
+```bash
+tmux new-window -a -t "$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION:{end}" -n "$TASK" -c "$WS_ROOT" -e HIVE_KICKOFF=... "$launch_cmd"
+```
+
+`-a` against `{end}` — the session's highest-numbered window — is append semantics: tmux allocates
+the next index *above* the last one, which is free by construction, so `create window failed: index
+N in use` cannot occur. The launcher supplies only the session and the window name (the task id).
+Two forms were deliberately rejected: an explicit derived index (the original defect), and a bare
+`-t <session>` with the index omitted — the latter still resolves to a concrete index. `{end}` was
+chosen over a bare `-a` because `-a -t <session>` inserts after the session's *current* window and
+shuffles every window above it up; `{end}` appends past the last, so no existing window moves.
+Nothing in the form depends on `base-index` or `renumber-windows`.
+
+**2. A pane failure after spine seeding is fail-safe, not archaeology.** Every post-seeding step —
+the kickoff-file write, `new-window`, `new-session`, and a new post-hoc assertion that the window
+actually exists — routes failure into a `half_launch` printer that exits non-zero after printing:
+the state (board owns the task on run X, only the pane is missing), the refusal to re-run
+`hive-launch`, the locations of both clones, the wrapper and the saved kickoff, the exact filled
+`tmux new-window`/`new-session` command that completes the launch, the kickoff text verbatim, and
+the abandon path (`task.reassigned` per RUNBOOK). The filled kickoff is now also written to
+`~/work/<worker>/kickoff.txt` on every launch, so the completion command reads it from disk instead
+of requiring a multi-line paste.
+
+**3. The one collision that remains meaningful — the name — refuses with its recovery path.** tmux
+itself creates duplicate window names happily (verified), so the pre-flight guard is the only thing
+keeping one task from having two panes. Its message now distinguishes a live/dead worker (kill the
+pane, then `task.reassigned`) from debris (kill the window, re-run the launch), and gives the
+`kill-window` command.
+
+**4. Drill coverage (`scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh`)** — a new section, *pane allocation: occupied
+indices, name collision, half-launch recovery*, with 22 assertions: the occupied-index reproduction
+(an explicit index still refuses on this tmux), a launch into that state allocating above the
+highest index while moving no existing window, a launch under `base-index 11` +
+`renumber-windows on`, the name-collision refusal (nothing provisioned, no board state, no second
+window), and the half-launch recovery print forced with a PATH shim that fails `new-window` with
+the historical message — no test seam in production code, since the launcher calls plain `tmux`.
+
+**5. The drill now runs on a private tmux server.** `TMUX_TMPDIR` points at the sandbox and cleanup
+is `kill-server`. This is a prerequisite for (4), not a bonus: the new cases occupy window indices
+and flip server-wide tmux options, and until now the drill created its session on the operator's
+default server — the one holding every live worker pane.
+
+**6. `RUNBOOK.md`** — "Dead worker recovery" gains a *Half-launched task* subsection (what it is,
+how to recognise it, why it is not a dead worker, the manual completion commands from memory, and
+the abandon path), and the drill sentence in the Phase 1 loop records the tmux isolation.

+## To operate
+
+- **Nothing to deploy.** Shell scripts on `PATH` only — no container surface, no compose, no env, no
+  service restart. Merge, and the next `hive-launch` uses the new path.
+- **Run the drill on the stack host after merging:** `scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh` from a clone
+  with the stack up. It now creates its own tmux server, so running it no longer touches the `hive`
+  session or its live worker panes — the previous behaviour was to create the drill session on the
+  operator's default server.
+- **Ordering: kept as it was — seed the board, then open the pane.** The order permitted reversing
+  it; this PR did not. Rationale: the worker's first act is `task.accepted`, which is legal only
+  after `task.assigned` has landed. A pane opened before the board writes starts a real session whose
+  first emit is rejected, and WORKER.md sends a worker that hits a rejection to report and end its
+  turn — trading a recoverable half-launch for a burned session. So the strand stays possible by
+  design, and the fix is that the launcher now hands over everything needed to finish by hand. Every
+  pre-existing refusal path is untouched: WIP throttle, board-state guards (adopt / owned / in_review
+  / done), clone clobber guards, dirty-order pin, and the pane-name guard all still fire before any
+  board write.
+- **New file per launch:** `~/work/<worker>/kickoff.txt` (the filled kickoff). It is removed with the
+  worker directory at the usual `rm -rf ~/work/<worker>` after close.
+- **If a launch half-fails,** the launcher prints the complete manual completion path; the same
+  procedure from memory is in RUNBOOK → "Dead worker recovery" → *Half-launched task*. Do not re-run
+  `hive-launch` on a half-launched task; it is owned and will refuse.
+- **The pane-name refusal message changed** (it now names the recovery path). Any operator habit
+  keyed to the old one-line text should key on "already exists" instead.
+
+## Reflection
+
+- **The index carries no meaning, so never name one — and "don't name one" is not the same as
+  "omit one".** Omitting the index still makes tmux resolve a concrete index; it just picks the
+  lowest free slot, which is silent, order-disturbing, and (per the 0727 evidence) not even reliably
+  collision-free. Only `-a` is allocation *by relation* rather than by number. The refinement worth
+  passing on: `-a -t <session>` alone appends after the *current* window and renumbers the operator's
+  windows out from under them — `{end}` is the form that appends and disturbs nothing.
+- **"The pane name is the registry" rests entirely on one `grep -qxF` in `hive-launch`.** tmux will
+  create a second window with the same name without complaint (verified). Phase 1 refuses a registry
+  file, which is right at this scale, but the refusal's whole enforcement is that guard — worth
+  knowing before anyone touches it, and worth remembering as an argument the day a real registry is
+  reconsidered.
+- **A drill that drives tmux on the operator's live server is a hazard the drill's own design
+  documented away.** It scrupulously isolated the workspace, the hub, the clones, the wrapper dir and
+  the run id — and then created sessions on the server holding every worker pane. The isolation
+  boundary was one item short of complete, and only a task that needed to make tmux *hostile* forced
+  the gap into view. The general lesson for the improver: an isolation list is a place where "all but
+  one" reads exactly like "all".
+- **A failure mode's fix can be a print.** Nothing about the half-launch was made impossible; the
+  launcher just stopped being the only thing that knew how to finish it. That was cheaper than any
+  transactional scheme (rollback of board writes, deferred seeding) and it leaves the state machine
+  alone — the alternatives all wanted to move authority around to save one manual step.
+- **Tension in the order, resolved by evidence:** the order asserts that the session-only form fails
+  identically to the explicit form, and the reproduction contradicts that on tmux 3.5a. The order also
+  anticipated exactly this ("if the drill can't simulate an occupied index portably, the report says
+  what was asserted") — the shape of the guidance held even where the specific claim didn't, which is
+  a good argument for orders naming their risks.
+- **Effort:** within the predicted 1–2 worker-hours; zero questions asked (the recovery-print format
+  was under-determined but reversible and operator-facing only, so it was decided in-bounds rather
+  than blocking).
+
+## Appendix — the reproduction harness
+
+Not committed: it is evidence tooling, not a second drill (the drill is the permanent home for these
+assertions). Two techniques make `hive-launch` runnable without the stack and without touching the
+operator's tmux; both are reusable for any future launcher work:
+
+```bash
+# 1. a private tmux server — every `tmux` call, including the ones inside hive-launch
+export TMUX_TMPDIR="$SANDBOX/tmux"; mkdir -p "$TMUX_TMPDIR"; unset TMUX
+
+# 2. a stubbed stack — hive-common's emit()/board reads go through `podman compose run ... cli`
+mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/bin" "$SANDBOX/omega"
+cat > "$SANDBOX/bin/podman" <<'EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in board-view) echo '[]'; exit 0;; emit) echo accepted; exit 0;; esac; done
+exit 0
+EOF
+chmod +x "$SANDBOX/bin/podman"
+export PATH="$SANDBOX/bin:$PATH" OMEGA_DIR="$SANDBOX/omega"
+```
+
+The rest of the fixture is the drill's own sandbox recipe (bare hub, workspace clone with
+`projects/alpha/{project.conf,orders/}`, a canonical code repo under `CANON_ROOT`, a `sleep`-based
+`HIVE_WORKER_CMD`), plus the hazard: build a session with a gap in its indices, select a window that
+is not the last, and launch into it. To force the half-launch, put a shim `tmux` first on `PATH`
+that fails `new-window` with `create window failed: index 4 in use` and `exec`s the real tmux for
+everything else.
